syllabus_topics: Molecular-kinetic description of liquids and solids
Dissolutions: Definition and molecular perspective of the process
Separation Processes: Crystallization and fractional distillation
Systems, states of matter and state functions
1st law of Thermodynamics: Heat and Work
2nd law of Thermodynamics: Entropy and Gibbs free energy
Free energy and the chemical equilibrium
Reaction quotient (Q) and estimation of reaction direction

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (lab practices, problem solving, topic tests, peer-corrected exercises)
Final exam (topics 4-7, potentially 1-3 if partial not passed)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on 15% continuous assessment and 85% exam. A mandatory nomenclature exam must be passed with at least 5/10; failure to pass after three attempts prevents passing the course, but its score does not contribute to the final grade. The exam consists of a partial exam (42% of the exam grade, topics 1-3) and a final exam (58% of the exam grade, topics 4-7). The partial exam is liberatory with a score of 5.5/10, requiring a minimum of 3.5/10 on the final exam; if the partial is not liberated, it must be re-taken during the final exam. Students must complete two mandatory lab practices; failure to do so results in failing the course. In the extraordinary call, students can choose between the same weighting as the ordinary call or a 100% final exam.
